gaps.explanation: The report prints two different amounts. The General Fund statement (trimmed p4) prints Capital outlay 251,888 and Total disbursements 2,333,816, with Operating Transfers Out (160,192). The all-funds budgetary comparison schedule (p8) prints Capital outlay 250,394 and Total disbursements 2,332,322, with Transfers In (out) (161,686). So 1,494 is capital outlay on p4 and a transfer on p8: 2,333,816 - 2,332,322 = 1,494 = 161,686 - 160,192. Every other line agrees. detail[] matches p8 as printed, so there is no fix.

This is the same 1,494 as the expenditure gap. The statement (p4) prints Operating Transfers Out (160,192) and the schedule (p8) prints Transfers In (out) (161,686), detail index 24: 161,686 - 160,192 = 1,494, which p4 counts as capital outlay (251,888 vs 250,394). The two printed totals really differ, so there is no fix.

The statement figure comes from the accrual proprietary Statement of Revenues, Expenses and Changes in Net Position (p6): Total Operating Disbursements 2,929,979 + Other Expense 9,640 + Interest expense 33,583 = 2,973,202 (includes depreciation 371,360 and amortization 154). The p8 budgetary schedule (cash basis) prints the Combined Utilities Fund Total disbursements as 2,973,719: Public works 2,929,979 + Capital outlay 3,051,197 + Debt service (3,007,457), where the debt service figure is net of the loan proceeds of 2,945,330 shown on cash flow statement p7. The schedule is on another basis than the statement, and 2,973,719 - 2,973,202 = 517. There is no fix.
